handoff.summary: Batch b04 (2 models): (12) CO2-equivalent on the 20-year horizon (CF4 AR6 values, explicitly not interchangeable with GWP100) and (13) recycling-only rate (69 Mt of 292.4 Mt, 23.6%) as a published subset headline distinct from the combined recycling-and-composting rate. Energy/volume EF bases and GTP endpoint metrics deferred with exact sources.

assumptions: Source assumption: GWP20 is the integrated radiative forcing over 20 years versus 1 kg CO2 (EPA GWP page; IPCC-TFI FAQ horizon concept); CF4 values are Sixth Assessment estimates for a gas with a 50,000-year lifetime.
application profile: single-gas conversion at the 20-year horizon; multi-gas sums at GWP20 need horizon-consistent components and are a separate aggregation.

gaps: Requires new quantity meanings for 20-year-horizon gas mass, GWP20 index and GWP20-based CO2e; units kg and 1 exist. Horizon carried in context, never interchangeable with GWP100.

models.inverse_notes: Mco2e with positive GWP determines Mgas = Mco2e / GWP; Mco2e with positive Mgas determines the implied GWP. GWP = 0 is only a zero-forcing idealization. Substitution checks: 10600 / 5300 = 2 recovers case cf4-large; 2650 / 5300 = 0.5 recovers case cf4-small. Algebraic only; GWP20 results must never be mixed with GWP100 inventories.
limitations: GWP20 prioritizes short-lived gases and must not be compared with, or substituted for, GWP100 results (CH4 81-83 at 20 years versus 27-30 at 100 years).
Excludes atmospheric physics, decay dynamics, discounting and offset claims.

references.method: EPA GWP page states CF4 has a 20-year GWP of 5300 (versus 7380 at 100 years); expected is independent multiplication 2 x 5300.
references.provenance: Published factor combined with independent multiplication; the total is derived, not source-published.

references.method: Same published CF4 GWP20 (5300) at a materially smaller mass; expected is independent multiplication 0.5 x 5300.

assumptions: Source assumption: numerator and denominator share the same reporting period, MSW scope and weight basis (EPA weight-basis post-consumer MSW scope).
Application profile: recycling-only subset headline; composting, other food management and combustion with energy recovery are excluded from this numerator by definition.

gaps: Requires new quantity meanings for recycled-only and total roles and the recycling-only rate; ledger mass unit t shared with b01. Scalar fraction fits the engine once meanings exist.

models.inverse_notes: Rr with positive Mt determines Mr = Rr x Mt; Rr with positive Mr determines Mt = Mr / Rr (needs Rr > 0). Rr = 0 with positive Mt implies zero recycling. Substitution checks: 0.2359781122 x 292.4 ~= 69 recovers case national-2018; 69 / 0.2359781122 ~= 292.4 recovers Mt. Algebraic only; stream eligibility follows the stated method.
limitations: Excludes composting and other recovery by definition; must be labeled recycling-only and never presented as the diversion rate.
A mass-based rate is not a GHG inventory; waste mass is activity data for separate factor-based estimation.

references.method: EPA National Overview 2018: about 69 Mt recycled of 292.4 Mt generated; fraction independently computed (69/292.4 = 23.6% when expressed as percent).
references.provenance: Values from published EPA figures; the fraction is independently computed, not source-published as a fraction.

references.method: Boundary identity: zero recycled mass gives a zero recycling-only rate at fixed generation.
references.provenance: Definitional boundary check; not an empirical validation.
